findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the signed read-set is projected from distinct_fetches: filter to read_file/list_directory path targets only (drop search_files query targets), normalize to repo-relative form (strip './', reject/relativize paths outside the repo), and state whether list_directory directory targets are dropped or expanded — so only hashable repo-relative file paths reach the ADR-0002 per-path check.
evidence: distinct_fetches append: {"tool": name, "target": target} where fetch_target returns the search QUERY for search_files and the path arg for read_file/list_directory
plan: 'Persist that read-set (repo-relative paths only)'
dependency_hashes hashes each path with _hash_file — a directory or a search query would hash to nothing/None, a dead leg that silently weakens the fail-safe
findings.finding: The plan feeds the read-set into the ADR-0002 per-path content-hash check as 'repo-relative paths only' but never specifies the filter/normalization that derives those paths from the telemetry source. distinct_fetches records {tool,target} where search_files targets are query STRINGS, list_directory targets are DIRECTORIES, and read_file targets may carry './' prefixes or reference paths outside the repo — none directly hashable as a repo-relative file.
findings.location: Plan component (a) 'the agentic passes already observe which repository files they open (distinct_fetches in telemetry)'; src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:197-221 (distinct_fetches shape), fetch_target 282-310
scenarios: A no-file-impact review that only ran search_files (no read_file) yields a read-set of query strings; after filtering to nothing, the deps set is globs-only even though the agent DID consult code
A read_file('./src/x.py') and a read_file('src/x.py') produce two entries for one file unless normalized, and one form may not match the hashing basis

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that blast-radius globs are expanded to concrete {path:sha256} deps at SIGN time and specify how additions/deletions under each glob are detected (e.g. hash a manifest/listing of the glob's matched set, or define _hash_file on a missing path as drift), so newly-added criteria/reviewer/gate files are not a currency blind spot.
evidence: compute_validity DEFAULT profile: 'drifted = [p for p, digest in sorted(deps.items()) if _hash_file(p, base=base) != digest]' — only paths already in the signed deps map are checked
dependency_hashes computes {p: _hash_file(p)} for p in a path set fixed at sign time
A glob names a SET whose membership can change (new .md reviewer, new gate .yaml); a per-path baked hash cannot detect an added member
findings.finding: The plan says the blast-radius globs are 'evaluated by the SAME per-path content-hash currency check ADR 0002 already ships', but that check iterates only the manifest's baked {path:sha256} deps map (compute_validity re-hashes manifest_deps). The plan never states that the globs are EXPANDED to concrete per-path hashes at SIGN time, nor how file-ADDITION/DELETION under a glob is caught — a file added after signing that matches a glob has no baked hash and will never register as drift.
findings.location: Plan component (b) 'evaluated by the SAME per-path content-hash currency check ADR 0002 already ships (no new diff walker)'; src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:568-576 (deps re-hash loop), manifest.py:324-352 (dependency_hashes)
scenarios: A new reviewer prompt src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_Z.md is added after a no-file-impact review is signed; it matches the glob but has no baked hash, so the currency check does not invalidate — the fail-safe the globs exist to provide misses the new criterion file
A blast-radius file is deleted after signing — _hash_file on a missing path must be defined to register as drift

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the derivation protocol reducing distinct_fetches to the signed read-set: which tools contribute paths (e.g. read_file only), how search_files query/pattern targets and list_directory directory targets are excluded or mapped, and that only existing repo-relative file paths enter the ADR-0002 dependency set.
evidence: Plan (a): 'The agentic passes already observe which repository files they open (distinct_fetches in telemetry). Persist that read-set (repo-relative paths only)'
Plan (b): the dependency set 'becomes read-set ∪ plan-cited paths ∪ the fixed blast-radius globs, evaluated by the SAME per-path content-hash currency check ADR 0002 already ships'

src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:282-310 fetch_target(): for search_files it returns the 'query'/'pattern'/'regex' STRING and for list_directory it returns a DIRECTORY path — only read_file yields a repo-relative file path ('search_files→its query/pattern, list_directory→its path')

src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:221 stores each entry as {'tool': name, 'target': target}; tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:281 pins distinct_fetches carrying a search_files entry whose target is a query string, not a path
ADR-0002 (docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md:27) and manifest.py:352 consume a {path: sha256} map of WHOLE-FILE hashes, requiring repo-relative existing file paths
By contrast the cited-paths side is precisely filtered: manifest.py:188-200 _cited_paths keeps only citations with kind=='file' and a path — the read-set has no analogous stated rule
findings.finding: The read-set is fed into the ADR-0002 per-path whole-file content-hash check as 'repo-relative paths only', but the plan never defines the protocol that derives those paths from the agentic passes' observation telemetry (`distinct_fetches`), which mixes repo file paths with non-path targets.
findings.location: Plan components (a) 'Record the review's read-set INSIDE the signed material' and (b) 'Feed the read-set into the ADR-0002 dependency set'
scenarios: A pass calls search_files(query='def compute_validity') and list_directory(path='src/rebar/llm/'); the executor must decide whether these enter the signed read-set and, if so, how a query string or a directory maps to a whole-file content hash.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the read-set is derived from distinct_fetches by keeping only tool=='read_file' entries (whose target is a repo-relative file path), normalizing a leading './', and dropping search_files query targets and list_directory directory targets; entries that do not resolve to an existing repo file are excluded — mirroring the kind=='file' filter _cited_paths already applies.

findings.finding: The blast-radius entries are GLOBS, but the reused ADR-0002 currency check is per-recorded-path (dependency_hashes stores concrete {path:sha256}; compute_validity re-hashes only those exact paths, with _hash_file mapping a missing path to _ABSENT_HASH). A glob expands to the files that exist at SIGNING time; a file newly CREATED under a blast-radius glob after review is never enumerated, gets no dep line, and its appearance is invisible to the per-path re-hash — so the design under-guards exactly the new-file churn the globs are meant to catch.
findings.location: Plan §Plan (b) ('evaluated by the SAME per-path content-hash currency check ADR 0002 already ships'; 'no new diff walker'); mechanism at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:324-352 (dependency_hashes) and 437, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:568-584 (compute_validity), _hash_file at manifest.py:175-185
findings.suggested_fix: Record the blast-radius glob PATTERNS (not just their signing-time expansions) in the signed manifest, and at currency time re-enumerate each glob against the current gate ref and hash the sorted (path, sha256) listing — so an added/removed file under the glob changes the listing digest and invalidates. Keep the file_impact/cited/read-set members on the existing per-path check unchanged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Describe the `review-plan --status` basis-reporting deliverable in the Plan body so AC4 maps to described work.
evidence: AC4: 'rebar review-plan <id> --status reports which basis (file_impact | read-set | fail-safe) currency was decided on'
Plan body (a)/(b) never mention a CLI status/basis-reporting deliverable
findings.finding: AC4 introduces a new CLI behavior ('rebar review-plan <id> --status reports which basis ... currency was decided on') that is not described anywhere in the Plan body (components a and b describe only the manifest read-set and the dependency-set feed) — an orphan criterion with no covering description.
scenarios: Implementer reads (a)/(b), builds the manifest+dependency-set change, and misses that a CLI reporting surface must also be added/modified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Give AC2, AC3, and AC4 concrete pytest invocations (e.g. a `-k` selector or named test module) that produce evidence on success, matching AC1's pattern.
evidence: AC1: 'python -m pytest tests/unit -k "attest and read_set" -x'
AC2: 'Verify: unit tests cover both directions through the existing ADR-0002 seam'
AC3: 'Verify: unit tests cover each fallback'
AC4: 'Verify: CLI output assertion in tests'
findings.finding: AC2, AC3, and AC4 state 'Verify: unit tests cover both directions' / 'unit tests cover each fallback' / 'CLI output assertion in tests' without a concrete runnable proving command, unlike AC1 which pins an exact pytest invocation.
scenarios: An executor cannot run AC2/AC3/AC4 verification without inventing a test selector, so 'done' is not deterministically provable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit commands, e.g. AC2/AC3: `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "currency and (readset or fallback)" -x`; AC4: `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "review_plan_status_basis" -x`.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] De-duplicate the blast-radius glob list (`.rebar/criteria_routing.json` appears twice), verify each glob resolves to files that exist (`src/rebar/llm/criteria/**` targets ids/model/overlay, not reviewer prompts), and state whether it reuses/derives from the existing criteria-routing path constant (scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py) rather than defining a second copy.
evidence: The plan lists `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` TWICE within the same glob set — a hand-assembled, unreviewed constant.

`scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:48-49` already hardcodes the routing-file set (`.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`); a second independent copy of overlapping 'review-config paths' can drift.

The list names `src/rebar/llm/criteria/**`, but `list_directory src/rebar/llm/criteria` shows only `ids.py, model.py, overlay.py, __init__.py` — the reviewer prompts actually live under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_*.md`, which the plan already names as a SEPARATE glob (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`); a glob targeting a dir whose contents don't match its evident intent is a cargo-cult signal.
The plan prose elsewhere writes `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria/**` (a third, differently-spelled nonexistent path), confirming the set was not verified against the tree.
findings.finding: The hardcoded blast-radius glob list is a newly-introduced constant that partially duplicates existing hardcoded 'criteria-routing path' sets and is internally inconsistent, risking a drifting second copy (config/constant proliferation + cargo-cult glob assembly).
findings.location: Plan §Plan component (b) — 'The blast-radius globs are named concretely: ...'
scenarios: A future criteria-routing path is added/renamed and updated in check_criteria_vocabulary.py but not in the currency blast-radius constant (or vice-versa), silently under- or over-guarding attestation currency.
The `criteria/**` glob matches zero (or the wrong) files, so an edit to an actual reviewer prompt does NOT invalidate a no-file-impact attestation despite the plan intending it to.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the duplicate `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` entry and the stale `src/rebar/llm/criteria/**` / `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria/**` spellings (reviewer prompts are already covered by `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`), and factor the routing-config paths from the single constant already used by check_criteria_vocabulary.py so the two lists cannot drift.

findings.suggested_fix: Include `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` in the blast-radius set (keep `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` too if overlay drift should also invalidate).
